verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit documents configurable rules that fire actions automatically on PR events. The reviews.auto_review settings control when reviews run: by keyword or label, by branch, skipping drafts, or pausing after a set number of commits. The request-changes workflow automatically requests changes or approves based on review outcomes, and CI/CD failures automatically trigger inline fix comments. However, the event types and actions are fixed and specific to code review, not a general user-defined event→action rule engine. missing for 10: arbitrary user-defined triggers and actions (custom event→action rules), documentation of an event catalog, independent or hands-on corroboration of the automation rules.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Configure when and how CodeRabbit automatically reviews pull requests using the `reviews.auto_review` settings.
you can disable reviews globally and re-enable them by keyword or label, apply them only to certain branches, skip draft PRs, and pause after a set number of commits
When enabled, CodeRabbit requests changes when a review posts actionable inline comments and approves the pull request after the approval requirements are met
When a CI/CD pipeline fails on a pull request, CodeRabbit reads the failure output and posts inline comments with suggested fixes
